<thought>Based on the mass spectrum, the molecular ion is at m/z ≈ 194.09 with an M+1 intensity of ~13 %, indicating roughly 11 carbon atoms. A plausible molecular formula that fits this mass and isotopic pattern is C₁₁H₁₄O₃ (exact mass 194.094 Da). This formula gives a double‑bond equivalent of 5, consistent with an aromatic ring (4 DBE) plus a carbonyl group (1 DBE). A common structure matching C₁₁H₁₄O₃ is **4‑hydroxy‑acetophenone** (para‑hydroxyacetophenone), whose SMILES notation is `CC(=O)c1ccc(O)cc1`. This molecule contains an aromatic ring, a carbonyl (ketone) attached to a methyl group, and a para‑hydroxy substituent, matching the inferred formula and unsaturation.
